name: WHO emergencies
summary: WHO's Bundibugyo Ebola emergency of international concern, declared 17 May, remains in force; no new PHEIC found
state: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak centred on DR Congo remains a public health emergency of international concern, declared on 17 May (WHO). WHO's Director-General briefed member states on it on 11 Nov, and WHO's Africa office said on 15 Nov that progress was fragile (WHO). Searches to 17 Nov found no new PHEIC in the past 30 days and no pandemic emergency, so a PHEIC in effect keeps Watch.
for_you: WHO's emergency declaration covers the Ebola outbreak in central Africa. Travellers to DR Congo and neighbouring countries should follow FCDO travel advice and NHS fit for travel guidance; UKHSA sets advice for returning travellers.
rubric_hit: A PHEIC in effect (Ebola, Bundibugyo virus, since 17 May) = Watch; no new PHEIC in past 30 days
basis_detail: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)
basis_by: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
